docs.title: 3. Hooks
docs.text:
Decision: the hub hooks ship in plugin hooks/hooks.json files. Each command reads its script through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.

Evidence:

  • hooks/hooks.json holds a top-level "hooks" key in the same shape as the hooks object in settings.json, so the hub entries copy in unchanged [docs: plugins/components#hooks].
  • A shell-form command wraps ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in double quotes [docs: plugins/components#environment-quoting-and-matching-mcp-tools].
  • Each hook process receives CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and one CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> per option [docs: plugins/manifest-reference#where-each-variable-resolves].
  • Plugin hooks register at load and fire on every matching event. They do not wait for a skill to run [docs: plugins/components#when-plugin-hooks-fire].
  • A hook in both settings.json and hooks/hooks.json runs twice per event [docs: plugins/create#convert-an-existing-claude-setup].
  • A plugin settings.json honors only agent and subagentStatusLine [docs: plugins/components#default-settings]. The permissions.ask rule for Bash(gh pr merge *) therefore stays a manual settings entry.
  • A [probe] loaded a SessionStart hook from hooks/hooks.json with a quoted ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} path.

Placement:

Hook script Event Plugin Toggle (userConfig, boolean) Default gh-check-before-create.sh PreToolUse Bash agenkic-ops enforce_naming true pre-push-auth.sh PreToolUse Bash, if: Bash(git push *) agenkic-ops pre_push_auth false. It switches the active gh account, which surprises a new user lint-precommit.sh PreToolUse Bash, if: Bash(git commit *) agenkic-ops lint_precommit true large-file-check.sh PreToolUse Bash, if: Bash(git commit *) agenkic-ops large_file_check true preflight-check.sh SessionStart agenkic-ops None Always on. It only warns python-syntax-check.sh PostToolUse Edit, Write agenkic-ops None Always on. It only reports context7-suggest.sh PostToolUse Read agenkic-ops None Always on. It only nudges stop-verify-gate.sh Stop agenkic-ops stop_verify_gate true continuous-learning-v2/hooks/observe.sh PreToolUse and PostToolUse, matcher * agenkic-ops observe_sessions false. It fires on every tool call agent-route-suggest.sh PreToolUse Agent, TeamCreate agenkic-core None Always on. It only nudges

Each toggled script reads its CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> value first and exits 0 when the value is false. Whether Claude Code exports an option the user never set, with its default, is [unverified]. Each script therefore treats an unset variable as the default in the table.

skills/ops/hooks/hooks.json, first entries:

{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/gh-check-before-create.sh\"", "timeout": 10 },
          { "type": "command", "if": "Bash(git push *)", "command": "bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/pre-push-auth.sh\"", "timeout": 15 }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Migration without double runs. Order matters. No session runs between the removal and the plugin install.

  1. Run setup/migrate-to-plugins.sh --dry-run. It lists each hub entry in ~/.claude/settings.json. It matches a hook command that ends in hooks/<name>.sh for the nine known names, in any directory. That match covers the symlink install and the copy steps in docs/patterns/hooks.md.
  2. Run the script without --dry-run. It writes a backup with the installer's .bak naming. It removes the matched entries with jq. It removes each ~/.claude/hooks/<name>.sh link that points into the repo. It keeps the permissions block.
  3. Run claude plugin install agenkic-ops@agenkic-hub and claude plugin install agenkic-core@agenkic-hub.
  4. Start a new session. Run /hooks or claude --debug to confirm one entry per event.

preflight-check.sh also warns at session start when settings.json still names one of the nine scripts. The plugin itself then reports a double wiring.

Rollback: claude plugin disable agenkic-ops@agenkic-hub, then copy the settings.json backup back. For one release, harnesses/claude-code/hooks stays as a symlink to ../../skills/ops/hooks/scripts. Old links into it keep resolving. That symlink sits outside every plugin root, so the plugin cache never sees it.

docs.title: 4. Workflows
docs.text:
Decision: the orchestration workflows move to skills/council/workflows/ as .js files. Nested calls use the namespaced workflow name.

Evidence:

  • Plugin workflows are .js files in workflows/ at the plugin root [docs: plugins/manifest-reference#standard-layout].
  • Plugin workflows run as /<plugin>:<meta.name> [docs: workflows#distribute-a-workflow-in-a-plugin].
  • A plugin demo.js ran as /agenkic-core:demo. A plugin demo2.mjs did not resolve [probe]. This matches the repo note that the name registry skips ~/.claude/workflows/*.mjs [repo: workflows/feature-loop.mjs:21-23].
  • claude plugin validate --strict passed a plugin with a .mjs workflow [probe]. Validation alone does not catch the extension.
  • workflow() takes a registry name or { scriptPath }. Nesting is one level deep. Scripts get no filesystem or Node.js API (bundled /workflow-authoring reference).
  • Inside a plugin workflow, workflow('agenkic-council:leaf', args) ran a workflow from a second plugin and passed args. A bare workflow('leaf') failed, and the error listed only namespaced names [probe].
  • ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} stayed literal inside a workflow script. The docs list no substitution for workflows [probe], [docs: plugins/manifest-reference#where-each-variable-resolves].
  • typeof process was 'undefined' inside the script [probe]. The current WF_DIR default therefore resolves to /.claude/workflows when the caller omits workflowsDir [repo: workflows/spec-loop.mjs:464]. That is a live bug.

Otherwise:workflow('agenkic-council:council-loop', a)` WF_DIR default process.env.HOME + '/.claude/workflows' Removed. The name path is the default feature-spec workflow meta.name: 'feature-spec' meta.name: 'spec-implement', see open question 4 Worked examples Shipped beside the tools docs/workflows/examples/, see open question 3 Smoke tests workflows/*.smoke.mjs tests/workflows/*.smoke.mjs. They stay .mjs, because Node runs them as modules Markdown in workflows/ feature-loop.md, spec-loop.md, spec-loop-spec.md docs/workflows/

A linked install keeps working. The workflows installer component points at skills/council/workflows/ until step M5. The .js files there also resolve by bare name for linked users [docs: workflows#save-the-workflow-for-reuse]. A linked install has no agenkic-council: name, so a linked user passes workflowsDir for the nested call.

Two points stay [unverified]. One is Workflow({ name, resumeFromRunId }) for a plugin workflow, because the reference shows resume with scriptPath. The other is the exact allow rule Workflow(agenkic-council:spec-loop) for claude -p.

docs.text:
No skill uses a {{variable}} template today. Only config/tmux/tmux.conf.tmpl and config/zsh/agentic-hub.zsh.tmpl do [repo]. The skills take settings as environment-style names in a "Configuration" section instead. userConfig replaces those names. The {{variable}} templates stay with the installer.

Evidence:

  • Types are string, number, boolean, directory and file. An unknown key inside an option fails validation [docs: plugins/manifest-reference#user-configuration].
  • An unset ${user_config.vault_path} stayed literal in the skill text [probe]. The result for "default": "" is [unverified].

docs.title: 6. What stays in the installer
docs.text:
The installer keeps every job that a plugin cannot do.

Component After the change config-tmux, config-zsh, config-statusline Unchanged ext-statusline, ext-tmux-theme, ext-dots Unchanged harness-codex, harness-opencode, harness-pi, harness-hermes Unchanged. Each gains a skills_dir= key once open question 10 settles skills-core, skills-council, skills-writing, skills-ops Link skills into the skills directory of each selected non-Claude harness. A new filter=SKILL.md key links only children that hold a SKILL.md. Without it, hooks/, workflows/, evals/, bin/ and commands/ leak into the targets workflows Removed in step M5. The plugin ships the workflows harness-claude-code Stops copying hooks into ~/.claude/hooks/. It prints the permissions.ask snippet to merge by hand New plugins-claude-code Runs claude plugin marketplace add and one claude plugin install agenkic-<group>@agenkic-hub per chosen group. --dry-run prints the commands New setup/migrate-to-plugins.sh The legacy cleanup in section 3, plus removal of hub skill and workflow links from ~/.claude/

The bash glob in link_children skips dot entries, so .claude-plugin/ never links [repo: setup/setup.sh:379]. setup.ps1 calls Get-ChildItem without a dot filter [repo: setup/setup.ps1:153]. The filter=SKILL.md key fixes both.

Codex and OpenCode keep the link install. A skill body that names ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} or ${user_config.*} reaches them as literal text. Each such line therefore keeps a harness-neutral fallback, such as a path relative to the SKILL.md or an environment variable.

Windows: plugins copy into the plugin cache, so Claude Code users no longer need the junction fallback [docs: plugins/loading#find-plugins-on-disk]. The Codex and OpenCode links on Windows still need it.

The author's own machine links ~/.claude/skills to the vault Skills directory, and the vault links each hub skill [repo: setup/relink.sh:12-13]. After the plugin install, every hub skill loads twice, once bare and once namespaced [docs: plugins/create#convert-an-existing-claude-setup]. Set each hub skill to "off" in skillOverrides in ~/.claude/settings.json. skillOverrides does not touch plugin skills [docs: skills#override-skill-visibility-from-settings]. Codex keeps reading the vault links.

docs.title: 7. CI
docs.text:
Two new jobs in .github/workflows/plugins.yml.

Job plugin-validate, on every PR:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.303
claude plugin validate . --strict
for p in skills/core skills/council skills/writing skills/ops; do
  claude plugin validate "$p" --strict
done
test -z "$(find skills -path '*/workflows/*.mjs')"
  • Given the marketplace root, validate checks the marketplace and the plugin.json of each relative-path plugin [docs: plugins/create-marketplace#problems-that-validation-reports].
  • Given one plugin root, it checks the manifest and the frontmatter of every skill, agent and command [docs: plugins/create#test-and-debug].
  • --strict turns warnings into failures [docs: plugins/cli-reference#plugin-validate].
  • The find line fails on a .mjs workflow, which validate lets pass [probe].
  • Whether claude plugin validate runs without credentials is [unverified]. Step M1 confirms it on the first CI run.

The existing ci.yml workflow job keeps its body-wrap syntax check. Its glob moves to skills/council/workflows/*.js in step M3.

Job plugin-eval, on PRs that touch skills/core/** and on manual dispatch:

claude plugin eval skills/core \
  --trust-plugin \
  --json results.json \
  --threshold 0.66 \
  --model claude-sonnet-5 \
  --no-publish \
  --max-cost-usd 5
  • Each case runs three times with the plugin and three times without it [docs: plugin-evals#how-a-case-is-scored].
  • --trust-plugin keeps CI off the trust prompt, and --json with a non-zero exit gates the job [docs: plugin-evals#run-evals-in-ci].
  • A threshold of 0.66 lets one of three runs miss.
  • A tool_used grader on Skill is a "plugin-fired indicator" in a two-arm run. It still counts when it is the only grader in a case [docs: plugin-evals#compare-against-a-no-plugin-baseline].
  • A no-trigger grader sets min: 0, max: 0 and arm: both, so the baseline arm scores it too [docs: plugin-evals#compare-against-a-no-plugin-baseline].
  • All graders are regex or tool_used, so no judge call adds cost [docs: plugin-evals#grade-the-result].

Skills under eval: brainstorm, feature-spec, context-handoff and agent-route. Claude invokes each one on its own. implement-spec and merge-next set disable-model-invocation: true, so a trigger eval says nothing about them [repo]. The four chosen skills have neighbors that compete for the same phrasing: brainstorm-grill, brainstorm and model-route.

Eight cases, one trigger case and one no-trigger case per skill:

Case Prompt (body of prompt.md) Graders brainstorm-trigger I want to add offline sync to our notes app. Before anyone writes code, can we think through the options and trade-offs together? Skill matches brainstorm. Skill matches brainstorm-grill with max 0 brainstorm-no-trigger Rename cnt to count in this line and show the result: let cnt = items.length Skill matches any agenkic-core skill with max 0. Reply matches count feature-spec-trigger We agreed the CSV export design: one button, server-side generation, a 10k row cap. Spec it out so we can build it. Skill matches feature-spec. Skill matches brainstorm with max 0 feature-spec-no-trigger In two sentences, what does a Gherkin Scenario Outline do? Skill matches feature-spec with max 0. Reply matches Examples context-handoff-trigger My context is long and I have to stop for today. Write a handoff so the next session can pick this up. Skill matches context-handoff context-handoff-no-trigger Which git command pushes my branch so a teammate can check it out? Skill matches context-handoff with max 0. Reply matches git push agent-route-trigger Which subagent type should investigate why our auth middleware returns 500 errors? Skill matches agent-route agent-route-no-trigger Which model tier fits a quick one-paragraph summary? Skill matches model-route. Skill matches agent-route with max 0

docs.title: Acceptance Scenarios
docs.text:
Feature: Hub Plugin Marketplace
  As a user of the hub
  I want one install command and marketplace updates
  So that hooks and workflows wire themselves and CI proves the package loads

  Background:
    Given Claude Code v2.1.303 or later
    And the user ran "claude plugin marketplace add Kiriketsuki/agenKic-hub"

  Rule: The marketplace installs and validates

    Scenario: Install the core plugin
      When the user runs "claude plugin install agenkic-core@agenkic-hub"

      And "/agenkic-core:feature-spec" starts the feature-spec skill

    Scenario: Strict validation fails on a bad manifest
      Given a plugin.json with an unknown key inside a userConfig option
      When CI runs "claude plugin validate . --strict"
      Then the job fails and names the field

  Rule: Cross-plugin references resolve

    Scenario: Council hands off to core

    Scenario: Core is missing

      When adversarial-council reaches its findings gate and the user answers y

  Rule: Hooks run once per event

      Then each hub hook runs once per matching event
      And a settings.json backup exists

      When Claude runs "git checkout -b wip"
      Then gh-check-before-create.sh exits 0

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
User Story: As a user of the council, I want one engine with one set of rules for review, fixes, pushes and liveness. Then I know which behavior runs, and a fix to the council lands in one place.

Problem: Four paths run the same review and fix loop. The adversarial-council, council-supervisor and council-fix skills drive an agent team by hand. The council-loop workflow drives scripted agents. Each path has its own fix, push and liveness rules. The supervisor reimplements stall detection that the workflow runtime now provides.

Out of Scope:

  • The internals of feature-loop.mjs and spec-loop.mjs. They keep their workflow() call to council-loop, and the new arguments default to the current behavior.
  • The review: 'budget' path in feature-loop.mjs and the critique phase in autofix-swarm.mjs. Both are small single-agent reviews. Open question 9 covers them.
  • Any change to the anti-gaming gate, the promote rule or the ledger of autofix-swarm.mjs.
  • A new council protocol. The engine keeps the exchange debate that council.debate: 'exchange' already defines.

docs.title: Success Condition
docs.text: This feature is complete when every council entry point runs its review through council-loop.mjs. No skill spawns a debate team by hand, and the workflow smoke suite passes with the same legacy prompt digest. The entry points are /adversarial-council, /council-fix, /council-supervisor, /parallel-fix --from-council, feature-loop, spec-loop and autofix-swarm.

docs.title: D2. Non-code motions
docs.text:
Decision: the engine grows a text mode. adversarial-council keeps no debate path of its own.

Shape: subject: { kind: 'text', motion, files }. motion is the proposition. files lists repo paths to read, such as a plan or an ADR. Text mode has these rules:

  • It needs council.debate: 'exchange' and fix: 'plan'. Any other combination fails at argument parse.
  • The review preamble tells agents to read the motion and the files. It runs no git diff and pins no branch.
  • A critic finding uses the document path as file, or an empty string, and line 0 when no line applies. The schema already allows both.
  • Evidence is a named source or a reasoning chain, as in evidence-protocol.md.
  • The arbiter rules FOR, AGAINST or CONDITIONAL. Its findings become action items. The run makes one convening and skips the Verify and Merge phases.

Why not a small text path in the skill: a text path in the skill needs its own debate. That means a team, a supervisor and a second set of rules. That is the duplication this feature removes. The text mode adds about 60 lines to the engine and reuses the exchange functions.

Cost: council-loop.mjs is already 904 lines, over the 800-line cap. Workflow scripts cannot import each other. Step M9 deletes the legacy parallel debate and pays the lines back.

docs.title: D3. Fix modes
docs.text:
The engine keeps two fix modes. A third value fails at argument parse.

Mode Engine behavior Who uses it fix: 'plan' One convening. No fix plan, fix or fix review agent. No commit, no push, no merge. A citation check labels each finding verified, unverified, phantom or runtime. The result carries a plan with blockers, non-blockers and phantoms. Verify still runs, so converged keeps its meaning. /council-fix, /adversarial-council by default, every text motion, the autofix-swarm backstop fix: 'auto' (default) Today's loop: fix plan, fix, fix review, semantic commit and push per round, re-review to an unconditional FOR, verify, optional merge feature-loop, spec-loop, /council-fix --auto, the wrapper after a y on a plan result

fix: 'plan' with merge: true fails at argument parse. The autofix-swarm backstop today fakes review-only mode with maxLoops: 1 and applyNonBlockers: false. It moves to fix: 'plan'.

Parallel competing fixes are not a council fix mode. The parallel-fix skill races minimal, refactor and rewrite strategies in worktrees and keeps the smallest passing diff. autofix-swarm.mjs already does this with more rigor. It adds an anti-gaming gate, an independent test re-run, a falsification set, a ledger and a stagnation pivot. Two copies of that race would drift.

So parallel-fix stays a separate skill and becomes a thin wrapper over autofix-swarm.mjs:

  • A direct call passes the bug as task.
  • --from-council <path> reads council-result.json. It groups the verified and unverified findings by file, at most five per group, and runs one swarm per group.
  • --strategies maps to fanout. The swarm clamps it to two or three.
  • --timeout maps to stallMs. Open question 4 covers the gap.
  • The "fresh rewrite" strategy becomes the swarm's alternative-root-cause. The synthesis agent becomes the swarm's council pivot.

It returns nothing to resume. Resume after the session ends claude --resume replays the run. Background sessions carry it over. Same gap as above for a fresh session Agent capacity check Concurrency cap of 16 with a queue. 1,000 agents per run. Stop at a usage limit Interactive runs pause until the reset, at most twice -p, the SDK and background sessions still fail. The engine stop stays.

Still missing after this feature:

  1. Hung tool calls. Time spent in an agent's own tool call does not count toward the stall window. A test command that hangs is never restarted.
  2. Fresh-session resume. The ledger lives only in the run. A new run re-reviews the committed branch from zero. A should-have arg council.seedLedger takes the ledger from a prior result.
  3. Mid-run input. The gate menu must sit between runs.
  4. Live view of the debate. The user sees agents in /workflows, not a message thread. log() lines carry the per-round counts.

docs.title: D5. Thin wrapper shape
docs.text:
Where it runs: in the main conversation. A skill with context: fork cannot launch a workflow, because Claude Code removes the Workflow tool from every subagent. The wrapper skills set no context key.

Invocation control:

  • adversarial-council stays model-invocable, so natural-language triggers keep working. Its default is fix: 'plan', which never edits the tree.
  • council-fix keeps disable-model-invocation: true. Its --auto flag commits and pushes, so only the user starts it.
  • A model-invoked wrapper never passes fix: 'auto' or merge: true unless the user typed that request in the current exchange.

Steps the wrapper follows:

  1. Parse the flags and the motion. Ask one clarifying question at a time when the target is unclear.
  2. Resolve the target. For a PR, run gh pr view <n> --json headRefName,baseRefName,state. Stop when the state is MERGED. For a text motion, collect the files.
  3. Detect buildCmd and testCmd with the table that parallel-fix uses today. Ask the user when none matches.
  4. Read the last .council/council-result.json for this slug into priorContext.
  5. Build the args. Pass objects, not a JSON string.
  6. Check that $HOME/.claude/workflows/council-loop.mjs exists. If not, tell the user to install the workflows component, and stop.
  7. Call Workflow({ scriptPath: "<absolute path>", args }). The path must be absolute, because the name registry does not resolve these scripts today.
  8. Tell the user the run started and that /workflows shows progress.

Permissions and approval:

  • The launch prompt follows the permission mode. Auto mode asks on the first launch only. Manual mode asks on every run. Bypass mode does not ask.
  • An allow rule Workflow removes the prompt. The README documents it as an option, not a default.
  • Workflow agents use the session permission rules. A run pauses on an agent permission prompt, so gh pr merge still waits for the user through the hook ask decision.

How results return: the run ends and its return value arrives in the session. The wrapper then does this:

  1. Write .council/council-result.json. Keep every field of today's schema and add runId, subject, fixMode, ledger and debateLog. Map the fields as follows. motion_type comes from subject.kind. verdict and conditions come from the final verdict. summary comes from its rationale. findings[].verification comes from the citation check. confidence and early_convergence become null and false.
  2. Write the recommendation markdown in FORMAT A for a diff or FORMAT B for text.
  3. Render the findings table or the action items table.
  4. Show the gate. On a plan-mode diff result, y starts a second run with fix: 'auto'. N records the result. modify asks for the new motion and starts a new plan-mode run.
  5. On a resumable stop, show the reason and offer a relaunch with resumeFromRunId.

Flag mapping:

Old flag New behavior --motion, --motion-file Diff target or subject.motion --n, --skeptic council.advocates, council.critics --rounds council.rounds, clamped --roles council.focus --model, --model-* council.model, with the engine floor --supervised Accepted. It prints a notice that the runtime supervises every run. --chain-fix After a plan-mode result, run /parallel-fix --from-council --heartbeat-interval, --max-nudges, --max-agents Accepted and ignored, with a notice --output Path of council-result.json

      When Claude invokes adversarial-council on its own
      Then the run uses fix "plan"

  Rule: Text motions use the same engine

    Scenario: Architecture decision
      When the user runs /adversarial-council --motion "Adopt event sourcing for orders"
      Then council-loop runs with subject kind "text"
      And no git command runs
      And the wrapper writes a FORMAT B recommendation with action items

    Scenario: Text motion with autofix is rejected
      Given args with subject kind "text" and fix "auto"
      When council-loop parses its args
      Then the run fails before any agent starts

  Rule: Existing callers keep working

    Scenario: feature-loop unchanged
      When feature-loop calls council-loop without a fix arg
      Then the fix mode is "auto"
      And the legacy prompt digest matches the stored digest

    Scenario: Old supervisor command
      When the user runs /council-supervisor --motion "Merge PR #7"
      Then the wrapper prints a deprecation notice
      And the council runs through council-loop

  Rule: Liveness comes from the runtime and the engine

    Scenario: Arbiter returns nothing
      Given the arbiter agent resolves to null
      When the engine reads the verdict
      Then the run stops with resumable true
      And nothing is merged

  Rule: Competing fixes use autofix-swarm

    Scenario: Chain from a council result
      Given a council-result.json with three verified findings in two files
      When the user runs /parallel-fix --from-council .council/council-result.json
      Then autofix-swarm runs once per file group
      And no candidate that touches a test file is promoted

docs.title: CLAUDE.md Curation
docs.text: CLAUDE.md files load into every Claude Code session in their scope. They are the docs with the most impact, and the easiest to ruin. This guide covers where they live, what belongs in each, and how to keep them short.

docs.title: The gitignored per-repo convention
docs.text:
Each repo carries its own CLAUDE.md at the repo root, and every repo gitignores it:

# .gitignore
CLAUDE.md

Why gitignore it:

  • It changes often and per developer, so it generates noisy diffs.
  • It may reference local paths, accounts, and machine details that do not belong in the repo history.
  • Tool-generated sections, such as a gitnexus index summary, rewrite themselves on reindex.

Version team-shared conventions in a committed file such as .github/copilot-instructions.md or CONTRIBUTING.md. CLAUDE.md can point at them.

docs.title: Workspace-level vs repo-level
docs.text:
Claude Code loads every CLAUDE.md from the current directory up to the filesystem root. A workspace root file and a repo file both apply, so split content by scope:

Scope File Contents Workspace <workspace>/CLAUDE.md Cross-repo conventions: git remote aliases, issue and branch workflow, versioning scheme, the repo directory map, package-manager policy Repo <repo>/CLAUDE.md This repo only: run and test commands, architecture summary, local conventions, gotchas

Never duplicate. A rule stated at workspace level does not repeat at repo level. Duplication drifts, and the two copies eventually disagree.

docs.title: What belongs in a repo CLAUDE.md
docs.text:
• Commands: how to install, run, test, and lint, with exact invocations.
  • A short architecture map: the main directories and what lives in each.
  • Conventions the model would otherwise guess wrong: naming, commit format, protected files.
  • Hard rules for tooling, such as a gitnexus impact-before-edit rule.

docs.title: What does not belong
docs.text:
• Anything the model can read from the code in seconds, such as a full API listing or a dependency inventory.
  • Long prose explanations. Link to a doc in docs/ instead.
  • Stale state: version numbers, TODO lists, sprint plans.
  • Generic advice the model already follows, such as "write clean code".

docs.title: Keeping them short
docs.text:
Every line costs context in every session. Budget accordingly:

  • Aim under about 100 lines for a repo file. A workspace file can run longer because it serves many repos.
  • Prefer tables over paragraphs. The model scans tables well.
  • Review the file whenever it misleads a session. A CLAUDE.md that caused a wrong action is a bug. Fix it the same day.
  • Delete before you add. When a section has not changed behavior in months, cut it or move it to docs/.

docs.title: Quick checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] CLAUDE.md is in .gitignore.
  • [ ] No content duplicated between workspace and repo level.
  • [ ] Every command in it runs as written.
  • [ ] No stale versions, paths, or plans.
  • [ ] Under about 100 lines, tables preferred.

docs.title: Claude Code Hooks
docs.text: Hooks are shell commands the harness runs around tool calls. They give you deterministic guard rails that do not depend on the model remembering an instruction.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event When it fires Typical use PreToolUse Before a tool call runs Validate, warn, or block the call PostToolUse After a tool call completes Auto-format, syntax check, reindex SessionStart When a session begins Environment health checks Stop When the agent finishes a turn Final verification, sync, cleanup

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Hooks live in ~/.claude/settings.json under the hooks key. Each entry names an event, a matcher, and one or more commands.
  • The matcher is a regex against the tool name. "Bash" matches Bash calls. "Edit|Write" matches both file-write tools. An empty matcher matches every tool.
  • The hook receives the tool call as JSON on stdin. A Bash hook reads .tool_input.command with jq. A file hook reads .tool_input.file_path.
  • Exit code 2 blocks the tool call. Write the reason to stderr. The harness shows stderr to the model, which can then retry correctly.
  • Exit code 0 lets the call proceed. The harness shows stdout to the model as feedback. Suggestion hooks use this to nudge without blocking.
  • A SessionStart hook must never exit non-zero. It reports, it does not gate.

docs.title: The absolute-path rule
docs.text:
Hook subprocesses run in a non-interactive shell. They do not load your .zshrc, so lazy-loaded tools such as an NVM-managed node are not on PATH, and ~ expansion is unreliable in some contexts. Two rules:

  1. Reference every hook script by absolute path in settings.json. Use $HOME/.claude/hooks/script.sh, not ~/.claude/hooks/script.sh.
  2. Inside a hook script, call binaries by absolute path when the tool is not in a standard system location. For example $HOME/.nvm/versions/node/{{node_version}}/bin/node.

docs.title: Wiring in settings.json
docs.text:
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "$HOME/.claude/hooks/gh-check-before-create.sh" }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "$HOME/.claude/hooks/python-syntax-check.sh" }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "$HOME/.claude/hooks/preflight-check.sh" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Example hooks
docs.text:
Guard rail: naming enforcement (PreToolUse, matcher Bash). Intercept git and gh create commands. Check branch names against <type>/<issue>-<kebab-description> and PR titles against the team convention. Exit 2 with a precise reason and a correct example, so the model retries with the right form.

Guard rail: pre-commit lint (PreToolUse, matcher Bash). Intercept git commit. Detect the stack from manifest files and run the project linter. Auto-fix and re-stage where the tool supports it. Unfixed errors block the commit with the full lint output.

Auth safety: push identity (PreToolUse, matcher Bash). Intercept git push, read the origin remote URL, and switch the active gh account to match the owner. Pair this with an SSH host alias per account, so the remote URL alone selects the right identity.

Correctness: Python syntax check (PostToolUse, matcher Edit|Write). Compile any edited .py file with py_compile. A syntax error exits 2, which forces a fix before the model moves on.

Reindex: gitnexus refresh (PostToolUse, matcher Bash). After git commit or git merge, rerun npx gitnexus analyze so the code intelligence index stays fresh.

Health check (SessionStart). Print structured [PREFLIGHT] lines: package-manager lock files, node availability, stale .git/index.lock files. Always exit 0.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Install the config-hooks component. It copies the scripts, the settings fragment, and the merge helpers into ~/.claude/hooks/:
./setup/setup.sh --components config-hooks
  1. Run the merge helper once. It backs up ~/.claude/settings.json to settings.json.bak, then merges the fragment entries in:
~/.claude/hooks/install-hooks.sh

& "$HOME\.claude\hooks\install-hooks.ps1"
  1. Restart Claude Code. Hooks load at session start.

The helper is idempotent. A second run reports zero changes and leaves the file byte-identical. Hooks you wired yourself stay untouched. See config/hooks/README.md for the script list and the removal steps.

The scripts require bash, jq, and git. On Windows, Claude Code runs hooks under Git Bash, so the same scripts work unchanged.

docs.title: Prose Linting with kilint
docs.text: kilint lints Markdown prose against the STE writing rules: short sentences, active voice, no semicolons, no em-dashes, no contractions, no filler. The tool lives in this repo at skills/writing/kilint/.

docs.title: Why lint prose
docs.text: Agent-written prose drifts toward slop: long sentences, hedging, filler phrases. kilint catches the form problems mechanically. A reviewer can then focus on whether the content is true.

docs.title: Run it locally
docs.text:
Lint one file:

python3 skills/writing/kilint/bin/kilint docs/tips/hooks.md

Lint a directory:

python3 skills/writing/kilint/bin/kilint docs/

Score a before/after delta when you rewrite a document:

python3 skills/writing/kilint/bin/kilint --delta BEFORE.md AFTER.md

docs.title: Rule families
docs.text:
Rule id Sentence length cap SEN001 Paragraph length cap STR001 No semicolon PUN001 No em-dash PUN002 No contraction WRD001 Active voice VRB001 No "-ing" main verb where a simple tense works VRB002 No nominalization WRD006 No phrasal verb WRD005 No marketing adjective WRD003 No filler phrase WRD004 One name for one thing TRM001

Code blocks, verbatim quotes, and vendored trees are exempt. The routing table in the shipped kilint.toml is the authority on exemptions.

docs.title: Score interpretation
docs.text:
kilint reports violations per 100 words.

  • Under about 1.5 violations per 100 words is clean. Merge it.
  • Above that, fix the flagged sentences and rerun.
  • Do not chase zero. A score of zero usually means you rewrote correct sentences to dodge the linter. The score is a signal, not a target.

kilint fixes the form of slop, not the content. It cannot make a hollow paragraph true. Review for accuracy separately.

docs.title: The CI gate
docs.text:
CI runs kilint on docs/ for every PR. The gate fails the build when a changed doc scores above the threshold. The workflow lives in .github/workflows/ and runs the same command you run locally, so a local pass predicts a CI pass:

python3 skills/writing/kilint/bin/kilint docs/

Run this before you push any docs change.

docs.title: Multi-Account Claude Code Setup
docs.text: Run a personal Claude account and a work Claude account on one machine. The account switches automatically based on the directory you launch from.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Claude Code stores identity, tokens, and session state in a config directory. The default is ~/.claude/. The CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable points Claude Code at a different directory. One directory per account gives you two isolated logins.

Account Config dir Workspace Personal, <you>@personal.com ~/.claude/ everywhere else Work, <you>@company.com ~/.claude-work/ {{work_workspace_root}}/**

Replace {{work_workspace_root}} with your work projects root, for example ~/work/company.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the work config directory
docs.text: mkdir -p ~/.claude-work

docs.title: Step 2: Add the switching function to zsh
docs.text:
Add this function to ~/.zshrc. It sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR inline at invocation, so the account follows your current directory:

unalias claude 2>/dev/null
function claude {
  if [[ "$PWD" == *{{work_workspace_root}}* ]]; then
    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude-work" command claude "$@"
  else
    command claude "$@"
  fi
}

The hub ships this fragment in config/zsh/. Do not use direnv for CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. A .envrc export has a timing race on first entry, so the variable may never reach the session. The function approach needs no shell restart and no per-directory setup.

docs.title: Step 3: Log in to the work account
docs.text:
cd {{work_workspace_root}}
claude
# Follow the login prompt. Authenticate as <you>@company.com.

docs.title: Step 4: Symlink shared resources
docs.text:
Keep only identity and state per account. Share agents, hooks, skills, and settings across both accounts with symlinks:

for dir in agents commands hooks rules skills plugins; do
  rm -rf ~/.claude-work/$dir
  ln -sf ~/.claude/$dir ~/.claude-work/$dir
done
rm -f ~/.claude-work/settings.json
ln -sf ~/.claude/settings.json ~/.claude-work/settings.json

What stays per account:

Path Why .claude.json OAuth account identity .credentials.json OAuth tokens history.jsonl session history sessions/, cache/, backups/ session state

Everything else is a symlink, so one edit applies to both accounts.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify
docs.text:
cd {{work_workspace_root}}
claude /config   # should show <you>@company.com
cd ~
claude /config   # should show your personal account

docs.title: Account-aware statusline
docs.text:
The templated statusline in config/statusline/ shows the active account and its usage. Two details matter:

  • Per-account usage cache. The statusline writes one cache file per config dir, for example /tmp/.claude_usage_cache_.claude and /tmp/.claude_usage_cache_.claude-work. Separate files prevent usage numbers from one account bleeding into the other.
  • Detect the account from $PWD, not from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Statusline and hook subprocesses do not inherit environment variables from the parent Claude session. The statusline script repeats the same workspace-path check the zsh function uses.

Fill in the {{template_vars}} in the statusline templates during setup/setup.sh, or by hand.

docs.title: Adding a third account
docs.text:
1. Create the config dir: mkdir -p ~/.claude-<name>.
  2. Log in once: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-<name> claude.
  3. Repeat the symlink loop against ~/.claude-<name>.
  4. Add a branch for the new workspace path to the claude zsh function.
  5. Add the matching branch to the statusline script.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• IDE extensions read ~/.claude/ide/ and ignore CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. IDE integration always uses the personal account. Terminal use is reliable.
  • claude --resume <id> resumes from the config dir active at launch, not the dir active when you created the session. Resume from the matching workspace directory.

docs.text:
Work in progress. Use this experimental tool for supervised development trials. Its interface can change. It is not a production supervisor or sandbox.

The launcher maps a TSV stream entry and Markdown brief to an existing Git branch, a worktree, a setup profile, and an interactive tmux window.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
The workflows/ directory holds background workflow scripts (.mjs) for multi-agent pipelines. Each script is a pure coordinator: it sequences agent(), parallel(), and workflow() calls, and every world-touching action happens inside an agent prompt.

Companion .md files (feature-loop.md, spec-loop.md, spec-loop-spec.md) document the driver patterns for their scripts.

Workflow Purpose ai-co-scientist.mjs Research hypothesis generation: generate, review, Elo tournament, dedup, and evolve, looped with a meta-review. autofix-swarm.mjs Autonomous fix swarm: diagnose, fan out competing worktree fixes, gate against gaming, promote a champion, and council-review. council-loop.mjs Standalone adversarial council fix-loop. Reviews a branch and drives it to an unconditional FOR verdict through fix rounds. feature-loop.mjs Per-feature build pipeline: brainstorm, spec, implement, council review, and merge, for one feature end to end. feature-spec.mjs Single-spec implementation with an adversarial quality harness: verify, implement, review, arbitrate, and fix. financial-data-pipeline.mjs Parses bank statement PDFs into a transactions dataset, consolidates to CSV, and runs Python EDA with charts. gmail-recurring-payments.mjs Crawls Gmail to surface recurring payments and subscriptions, then synthesizes a monthly-equivalent spend list. spec-loop.mjs Decomposes a whole spec into a routed dependency DAG, builds leaves in parallel worktree waves, and councils every PR. spec-loop.smoke.mjs Test harness for the workflow suite: syntax-checks the scripts and asserts the pure helper functions. spending-habits-categorizer.mjs Crawls bank statements in cloud storage, parses transactions, and categorizes a year of spending into a habits report. ultracode-fix.mjs Tiered fix pipeline: explore, plan, fan-out implement, and review, with fixed model assignments per phase. ultracode-implement.mjs Sibling of ultracode-fix aimed at building a feature instead of fixing a defect. Same tiered pipeline.
